events.title: English Language Learners' (ELL) Conversation Club (via Pearl and Cambrian)
events.description: San Jose Public Library presents an English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club that creates a welcoming and respectful environment for adult learners of English to practice their English conversation skills. Club meetings will convene online each week with our Pearl Avenue librarians and an ELL facilitator on Tuesdays, 11:00 a.m. - 12:00 pm. Test your English skills with others who are learning English, too. Everyone is welcome! Please register by clicking on the Register button. When you give us your email, we are able to send you a link to the Zoom meeting on the day of the program. Usually, the links will arrive about 30 minutes before the class begins.

events.title: Civic Literacy: Vocabulary for Voting
events.description: Learn vocabulary to help you vote! Together we will: Read an Easy Voter Guide for the November 2026 California General Election. Define important words and civic concepts. Understand the propositions on the ballot. Oct. 6: Intro to General Election & Offices; Oct. 20: Tax Propositions (Prop 40, 41, 42, 43); Oct. 22: Bonds & Tax Propositions (Prop 1, 2, 3, 37, 38); Oct. 27: Elections & Agencies (Prop 4, 5, 39, 44, 45). These workshops are an opportunity to practice reading, learn about American civics, build your English vocabulary, and prepare for voting in general elections. Free. Registration required. Presented in English.
events.blurb: Join online to read an Easy Voter Guide and learn the vocabulary behind this election's propositions.

events.title: Finding Stillness: Letting go of Anxiety through Meditation
events.description: Meditation offers a quiet refuge from the noise of anxious thoughts, helping you return to the present moment with greater ease. By stilling the mind and body, you create space between yourself and the worries that often feel overwhelming. This practice can soften the intensity of anxiety, improve emotional wellbeing and build a sense of inner calm. Even a few minutes a day can become a powerful tool for grounding, clarity, and resilience in the face of life's uncertainties. There will be a chance to practice this technique. Join Arlene Samsel for this workshop. Brief bio of Arlene Samsel: Arlene Samsel is uniquely qualified and experienced in meditation, public speaking, and the performing arts. She has been an elementary school teacher and has also performed publicly as a musician for many years. In addition, Arlene was director of a camp where she taught children how to meditate. She has been meditating for 25 years and has given many meditation workshops and retreats which have enabled her to speak firsthand about the crucial role of meditation in enhancing the daily lives of busy people. Arlene and her husband have raised a family of 3 children and reside in New Brighton, Minnesota.
events.blurb: Join an online meditation session where you practice stilling the mind and body to ease anxious thoughts and return to the present.

events.title: Short Story Social: "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" by Jeanette Winterson
events.description: Love the idea of a book club but don't have time for a whole novel? Join our Short Story Social, a relaxed "book club" for short-story fans and busy readers. We meet virtually on the last Thursday of each month to discuss one or two contemporary short stories (no more than 40 pages total). Participate from anywhere—jump in late or leave early if needed! Registration is required to receive the Zoom meeting link. 2026 Reading List: June 25th - "The Shroud" in Heart Lamp by Banu Mushtaq; July 23rd - "Mall of America" by Suzanne Wang in The Best American Short Stories 2024; August 27th - "A Sunny Place for Shady People" in A Sunny Place for Shady People by Mariana Enriquez; September 24th - "Dominion" by Lauren Acampora in The Best American Short Stories 2025. * Also available in New England Review, Vol 45, No. 2 - available through Gale Academic Onefile with your library card. October 29th - "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" in Night Side of the River by Jeanette Winterson
events.blurb: Join an online short-story book club on Thursday evening to discuss Jeanette Winterson's "A Fur Coat" and "Boots" with fellow readers.

events.title: AI Literacy & AI Bias
events.description: How can we use artificial intelligence responsibly? Join us for a free, interactive 60-minute session about AI literacy and bias. Participants will learn how bias can enter AI systems, how AI can affect different communities, and how to recognize misinformation, hallucinations, and unfair results. No previous AI or coding experience is required! This workshop is led by Together We AI, a nonprofit organization that aims to make AI education accessible to everyone.

events.title: Tech Mentor / Computer & iPad Assistance
events.description: Tech mentoring and computer 1-on-1 assistance. A volunteer tech mentor / computer coach will be available to help customers increase their computer skills. Are you a senior trying to catch up with the digital world? Would you like to learn how to create an email, to search the internet, to create and edit Microsoft Word documents, to do online job searching or to complete online job applications? Increase your digital literacy today. Our tech mentors can guide you in learning a variety of computer skills that enable you to better use the library's public computers and to benefit from the library's freely available online resources, including ebooks! Don't worry about not having a computer; iPads will be available for in-library use during the mentoring session. Our tech mentor is available on a drop-in schedule. If you have more questions, please call us at 408-808-3053.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one computer and iPad help from a volunteer tech mentor who can help you build your skills.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club
events.description: Boost your English conversation skills with our volunteer instructor, Ms. Veena, in a welcoming and respectful setting tailored for adult learners. Improve your speaking and listening abilities, broaden your vocabulary, participate in discussions on current events, and more—all at no cost. Pre-registration is required to receive reminder emails and lesson plan details. Due to limited capacity, please arrive on time. If you are more than 5 minutes late, your spot may be given to someone on the waitlist. Thank you for your understanding. Sessions are held weekly in the library's Group Study Room.
events.blurb: Practice conversational English with volunteer instructor Ms. Veena and discuss current events with fellow adult learners.

events.title: Reading Buddies
events.description: Reading Buddies provides students in grades K-3 with an opportunity to improve their reading skills by working one-on-one with a reading coach. Reading Buddies creates a positive reading experience for beginning and developing readers and helps children build confidence as readers. Our reading coach will listen to children read and provide support in reading and comprehension. Students can bring their favorite book or choose from the available selection at the Joyce Ellington Branch Library. Free. Pre-registration not required. However, reading sessions are available on a first-come, first-served basis and the duration of reading sessions may be limited depending on the number of participating students.
events.attendanceNote: Free. Pre-registration not required. However, reading sessions are available on a first-come, first-served basis and the duration of reading sessions may be limited depending on the number of participating students.
events.blurb: Watch K-3 readers pair with coaches for one-on-one practice at Reading Buddies at Joyce Ellington Library.

events.title: Math Workshop
events.description: This math workshop is geared towards middle schoolers; however, younger children who are passionate about math are also encouraged to participate. Develop your mathematical understanding with fun workshop activities! Students will share their strategies and thinking with each other during the workshop to foster discussion. The focus will be on developing mathematical understanding over memorization. This volunteer-led program will include concept review, independent work time, group discussion, and solution sharing. The topics of this workshop will be: counting and combinatorics.
events.blurb: Work through hands-on math activities designed for middle schoolers and eager younger kids alike.

events.title: Music and Movement in Vietnamese and English and Craft / Múa Hát Song Ngữ Anh
events.description: Bilingual Music and Movement in English and Vietnamese is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities through songs, rhymes, finger plays, and movement activities both in English and Vietnamese. Music and Movement is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning for all ages. This program is geared for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! Following the Storytime, kids will learn to make a simple and creative craft to take home! We host Vietnamese Storytime and Craft every Friday, plus a special bilingual session on the fourth Tuesday of each month. Free, no registration is required. Please note that this will be an indoor program. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards. Múa hát song ngữ bằng tiếng Anh và tiếng Việt được thiết kế để phù hợp với nhiều lứa tuổi. Chúng tôi mong muốn mời cả gia đình cùng tham gia vào các hoạt động này để cùng hát các bài đồng dao, cùng vận động ngón tay và cùng nhảy múa vui vẻ. Âm nhạc và nhảy múa là một trải nghiệm thú vị và giúp cho cả gia đình tương tác tốt hơn, thúc đẩy niềm vui học tập cho trẻ em ở mọi lứa tuổi. Mọi người đều được nhiệt liệt chào đón tại chương trình này. Sau phần kể chuyện, các bé sẽ được hướng dẫn làm một món thủ công đơn giản và sáng tạo để mang về nhà! Thứ Sáu hằng tuần có hoạt động kể chuyện và thủ công tiếng Việt; riêng thứ Ba tuần thứ tư hằng tháng sẽ có chương trình kể chuyện song ngữ đặc biệt. Chương trình hoàn toàn miễn phí và không cần phải đăng ký trước.
events.blurb: Sing, dance, and play along with bilingual English and Vietnamese songs and early literacy activities.

events.title: Reading Partners One-on-One Reading Tutoring
events.description: Free Reading Help for Students in Grades 1–3. Recommended for students in 2nd and 3rd grade. Give your child extra support to become a stronger, more confident reader! Reading Partners provides free one-on-one reading tutoring with trained volunteer tutors. Students meet twice a week for 45-minute sessions and receive personalized, research-based reading support. Program Dates: September 21, 2026 – May 28, 2027. Space is limited, and applications are reviewed to determine if the program is a good fit for your child. Apply Online — It's Free! Ayuda de lectura Gratis para estudiantes de 1.º a 3.º grado Recomendado para estudiantes de 2.º y 3.º grado. ¡Brinde a su hijo/a apoyo adicional para que se convierta en un lector más seguro y exitoso! Reading Partners ofrece tutoría de lectura individual y gratuita con voluntarios capacitados. Los estudiantes se reúnen dos veces por semana en sesiones de 45 minutos y reciben apoyo personalizado de lectura basado en investigaciones. Fechas del programa: 21 de septiembre de 2026 – 28 de mayo de 2027. El espacio es limitado y las solicitudes serán revisadas para determinar si el programa es adecuado para su hijo/a. Hãy giúp con quý vị nhận thêm sự hỗ trợ để trở thành một người đọc tự tin và thành công hơn! events.title: Forgotten Voices: Italian Americans Uprooted in Wartime California
events.description: Dive into a lesser-known chapter of American history: the experiences of Italian Americans on the West Coast during World War II. Through archival photos, historical context, and personal storytelling, Lindsay examines the impact of Executive Order 9066 on Italian American communities, especially in the Bay Area. Learn about surveillance, civil rights violations, and the long-buried trauma passed through generations. Highlights include: the little-known internment of Italian Americans alongside Japanese and German communities; the devastation of family-run industries like fishing in California; stories of resilience, cultural erasure, and rediscovery; legislation and resolutions acknowledging past injustices. Lindsay Marie Morris is a novelist and journalist based in Los Angeles. Her novels are inspired by her Sicilian-American roots and are grounded in years of historical research, from family archives and oral history interviews to wartime records and on-the-ground exploration in her novel settings. All are welcome. No registration needed. This program celebrates Italian-American Heritage and Culture Month. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.
events.blurb: Learn about the World War II experiences of Italian Americans on the West Coast at Cupertino Library.

At our meetings we present programs which encourage and inspire members to explore new techniques in needlepoint, learn about design, color, texture and perspective, and provide an opportunity to network with others who share a passion for needlepoint. events.title: Forgotten Voices: Italian Americans Uprooted in Wartime California
events.description: Dive into a lesser-known chapter of American history: the experiences of Italian Americans on the West Coast during World War II. Through archival photos, historical context, and personal storytelling, Lindsay examines the impact of Executive Order 9066 on Italian American communities, especially in the Bay Area. Learn about surveillance, civil rights violations, and the long-buried trauma passed through generations. Highlights include: the little-known internment of Italian Americans alongside Japanese and German communities; the devastation of family-run industries like fishing in California; stories of resilience, cultural erasure, and rediscovery; legislation and resolutions acknowledging past injustices. Lindsay Marie Morris is a novelist and journalist based in Los Angeles. Her novels are inspired by her Sicilian-American roots and are grounded in years of historical research, from family archives and oral history interviews to wartime records and on-the-ground exploration in her novel settings. All are welcome. No registration needed. This program celebrates Italian-American Heritage and Culture Month. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@lib.sccgov.org.

events.title: Volunteer Away Your Fines
events.description: Every now and then, libraries need a little extra love from the communities they serve. You can volunteer away your library fines at a rate of $20 per hour while helping the library maintain a clean and welcoming environment. Volunteers will be responsible for: Book cover cleaning – Use disinfecting wipes to reinvigorate dingy books. Bookshelves – Dust shelves and organize library materials. Deep cleaning computers – Use disinfecting wipes to disinfect computer mice and mouse pads and compressed air to remove any dust particles or debris. Material inspection – Check books for torn pages, pen marks, etc. This is a perfect opportunity for anyone interested in volunteering away their library fines. Details and Requirements: Must be able to commit to the full session; Anyone under the age of 15 must volunteer alongside a parent/guardian; No experience or special skills necessary; Training and supplies will be provided. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: Please register online or ask for assistance by calling/visiting our Information Desk. Space is limited.
events.blurb: Volunteer at Calabazas Library to work off your fines at $20 per hour while helping keep the space clean and welcoming.

events.title: Baby Lap-Sit Story Time
events.description: This program is geared for pre-walking children and their parents or caregivers. Baby Lap-Sit Storytime invites newborns, infants, and their caregivers to learn together by strengthening their relationship with each other through stories, songs, bounces, tickles, rhymes, books, and play. The program includes 20-25 minutes of stories and songs, followed by 40 minutes of open play with age-appropriate toys. All attendees will be required to observe the library's Safety Guidelines. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.blurb: Bring your pre-walking baby to listen to stories and rhymes built for little ones.

events.title: Halloween Program & Costume Parade
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Get ready for a ghoulishly good time at Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Library! Here's what's brewing for this not-too-spooky Halloween event: Showtime at 4:00 PM: Kick things off with an outdoor performance with Andy Z (bring a cozy blanket or mat for sitting). Meet at the Campus Entrance to start the fun! Parade after the show: Line up on the first floor for a fun costume parade through the library's first floor, with an option to continue the parade by Trick-or-Treat stations up to the 3rd floor. (Escalators and elevators are available.) More fun after the parade: Each child can grab a free book and enjoy a Scavenger Haunt in the Children's Room. Costumes are welcome and encouraged (but not required). This event is perfect for little monsters and their families.
events.blurb: Watch an outdoor performance by Andy Z and join the costume parade at a not-too-spooky Halloween program at King Library.

events.title: Fuse Bead Crafternoon
events.description: Design and create small artworks using fuse beads (also known as Perler beads)! In this workshop participants will create their own artwork using colorful fusion beads. This program introduces simple designs, pattern-building, and color planning. Participants can follow ready-made templates or create their own designs. After building their designs on the pegboards, we will safely fuse the beads with heat so everyone can take home their finished design for themselves or others. Registration required: supplies are limited! Recommended for ages 7 and up. Caregivers are welcome to join; younger children may need assistance from an adult. Tarde de manualidades: ¡Magia con cuentas de fusión! ¡Diseña y crea pequeñas obras de arte con cuentas de fusión (también conocidas como Perler Beads)! En este taller, los participantes crearán sus propias obras de arte con cuentas de fusión de colores. Este programa introduce diseños sencillos, creación de patrones y planificación de colores. Los participantes pueden seguir plantillas prefabricadas o crear sus propios diseños. Después de construir sus diseños en los tableros perforados, fusionaremos las cuentas de forma segura con calor para que todos puedan llevarse a casa su diseño terminado, ya sea para sí mismos o para otros. Se requiere inscripción: ¡suministros limitados! Recomendado para niños a partir de 7 años. Los cuidadores pueden participar; los niños más pequeños podrían necesitar la ayuda de un adulto.
events.blurb: Make small artworks from fuse beads, working on simple designs, pattern-building, and color planning.

events.title: One-On-One Tech Help (English or Tiếng Việt)
events.description: Offered in English or Tiếng Việt. Do you need help using a computer? Want to set up an email account? Stop by the Santa Teresa Branch Library for a session with our experienced volunteer! They can assist you with basic tech issues, such as: Setting up an email account, composing & sending emails, using email attachments; Web searches and basic data entry; Learning the basics of Microsoft Word and Excel and web-based productivity software such as Google Docs; Using the library's pay-for-print and photocopy machines; Downloading apps on your phone or tablet; And much more! You are welcome to bring your own device, such as a laptop, phone or tablet, or you can use one of our computers. Free. No registration required.
events.attendanceNote: Drop-ins subject to availability.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one computer help from an experienced volunteer, offered in English or Tiếng Việt, such as setting up an email account.

events.title: Reading to Children
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. Children will enjoy one-on-one or small group interaction with our volunteer. They are also welcome to practice reading to our volunteer. Pre-registration is not required, and children may drop in to hear a story any time during the program. This program is best suited for preschoolers and children in grades K to 3 and will be held in the Children's area. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Bring your child to Alviso Library for one-on-one reading time with a volunteer.

events.title: ESL Classes with Evergreen Valley College (EVC) - ESL 501: Reading & Writing 1
events.description: Develop your English language skills by practicing speaking, listening, reading, writing, vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar. Do you want to build your English language skills and your confidence? This beginning non-credit ESL course is Free! ESL 501 Reading & Writing 1. What will you learn in this class? This is a non-credit, high-beginning-level integrated ESL skills course emphasizing basic reading, writing, grammar, and vocabulary. Students will learn to comprehend frequently used words in context, use learned phrases and sentences to express ideas in basic writing, understand basic grammar structures, and read simplified material. Course Information: Starts: August 25, 2026; Ends: December 10, 2026; Meeting Days: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday; Time: 10:30 AM - 12:30 PM; Instructor: Michelle N. Henninger. Before the classes start, you must complete a Guided Self-Placement (GSP). This is not a test—it's simply an assessment to help us place you in the most appropriate ESL class based on your current English level. We will assist you with the application and registration process in person at the Edenvale Branch Library. Space is limited.
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited.
events.blurb: Practice speaking, listening, reading, writing, vocabulary, pronunciation, and grammar in a free beginning ESL course, ESL 501 Reading & Writing 1.

events.title: Halloween Baby / Toddler Storytime & Parade
events.description: Join us for a Halloween story this week, and wear your favorite costume, if you'd like! After storytime, we will have a short costume parade and trick-or-treat through the library! Baby/Toddler Storytime invites children and their caregivers to wiggle, rhyme, and sing with diverse books, songs, and fingerplays that encourage language, play, and exploration. This program is geared for children 0 to 3 years of age and their parents/caregivers, but all children are welcome! Free, with limited capacity. Seating for storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of storytime. Child must be present to receive a ticket. San José Public Library Storytimes are in alignment with the City's Education and Digital Literacy Initiative.
events.attendanceNote: Free, with limited capacity. Seating for storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of storytime. Child must be present to receive a ticket.
events.blurb: Listen to a Halloween story at Vineland Library, then join a short costume parade and trick-or-treat through the library; costumes are optional.

events.title: STEM Wednesdays: Code Your Cauldron - A Halloween Potion project (in Scratch)
events.description: Students will use Scratch to code their own magical cauldron that changes color and makes spooky sounds whenever an ingredient is clicked! Through hands-on activities and interactive questions, students will learn coding concepts like sprites, events, and sounds while creating their own potion projects. At the end, students can show off their creations to parents and Wi STEM members, and there will be candy provided. Recommended for ages 5-11. Free. Registration required (drop-ins accepted, provided there is space). Brought to you by Harker Women in STEM (Wi STEM)
events.blurb: Code a Halloween cauldron in Scratch that changes color and makes spooky sounds whenever you click an ingredient.

events.title: Infant & Toddler Storytime
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: Infant and Toddler Storytime invites children and their caregivers to wiggle, rhyme, and sing with diverse books, songs, and fingerplays that encourage language, play, and exploration. This program is geared for children 0 to 3 years of age and their parents/caregivers, but all children are welcome! After Storytime concludes, we invite you to Stay & Play! Until 12 PM the Storytime librarian and special toys will be on the Children's Room floor to keep the fun going. Meet new friends, play with toys, chat, get book recommendations, and maybe even create something! Storytime: 11:00-11:30 AM; Stay & Play: 11:30 AM-12:00 PM. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.blurb: Wiggle, rhyme, and sing with your infant or toddler through books and fingerplays at this storytime.

events.title: Reading Buddy in English & Spanish
events.description: Help your child build confidence and strengthen their English or Spanish reading skills in a fun and supportive environment! Children in kindergarten through 3rd grade are invited to read aloud in English or Spanish to trained teen volunteers who will offer encouragement and help with pronunciation when needed. Whether your child is a fluent English or Spanish reader or is still building their confidence, Reading Buddy in English and Spanish provides a welcoming space to practice reading skills, celebrate bilingual literacy, and foster a lifelong love of reading—especially for students enrolled in dual-language immersion programs. Recommended for: Children in grades K–3 and their caregivers. Please note: Caregivers must remain in the Children's Area during the program.
events.blurb: Read aloud in English or Spanish to trained teen volunteers at Willow Glen Library's Reading Buddy program.

events.title: English Language Learner (ELL) Conversation Club: Intermediate
events.description: ¡Ven a practicar hablar y escuchar inglés en persona en la Biblioteca Latinoamericana! Desarrolla habilidades de conversación con otros estudiantes de nivel intermedio en un lugar acogedor y respetuoso. Este programa es para adultos solamente. Cada sesión está dirigida por personal de la biblioteca que habla español y inglés. Gratis. No es necesario registrarse. Come practice speaking and listening in English in-person at the Biblioteca Latinoamericana! Build conversation skills with other intermediate level adult learners in a welcoming and respectful environment. Each session is led by library staff who speaks Spanish and English. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Practice intermediate English conversation with fellow learners at Biblioteca Latinoamericana Library.

events.title: Intro to Ukulele for Adults
events.description: In this 3-part series for adults, participants will learn the basics of playing the ukulele, will acquire the ability to read chords, get hands-on experience with the instrument, and learn some rudimentary concepts of music theory. The series will include 3 sessions, and each session will cover the following: Session 1 (10/14): Chords & how to read them; How to hold & strum the ukulele; Tuning; Session 2 (10/21): Review chords & introduce 3 finger chords; Introduce rhythm patterns. Session 3 (10/28): Practicing rhythm patterns; putting it all together; advanced techniques. No musical experience required. Ukuleles will be provided to participants, but you may bring your own if you have one. Registration is required. Registration opens in September and closes the day before the first session. Limited to 10 seats. Join the waitlist if the registration is filled. We recommend that participants come to all three sessions.
events.blurb: Learn basic ukulele chords, strumming, and music theory basics in this hands-on adult series.

events.title: 3D Printer Escape Room: Spooky
events.description: Can you crack the codes and escape in time? Put your problem-solving skills to the test in our 3D Printer Escape Room. Work together to solve riddles, uncover clues, and unlock a series of puzzles featuring 3D-printed objects. You'll need teamwork, creativity, and a sharp eye to complete the challenge before time runs out! This month's theme is Spooky. Each month features a new theme and challenge, so come back and see if you can escape them all. For middle and high school students. No 3D printing experience is required. Request ADA accommodations for this event.
events.blurb: Solve riddles, uncover clues, and unlock puzzles built around 3D-printed objects as a team in a spooky escape room.

events.title: Indoor Music and Movement
events.address: 150 E San Fernando St San Jose
events.description: This program is best for children ages 2-8 with their caregivers, but all children with caregivers are welcome. Join us every Wednesday for Music and Movement at the King Library Children's Room! Music and Movement is designed to accommodate a mix of ages; we invite the entire family to participate in early literacy activities and develop motor skills through song and movement activities - sometimes with scarves, shaky eggs, and rhythm sticks! Music and Movement is a high energy Storytime - a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of learning and movement. We'll start with a story, then move and groove to our monthly playlist. Free, with limited capacity. Program finishes by 6:10 PM. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.blurb: Sing and move along with other kids and caregivers at Wednesday Music and Movement in the Children's Room.

events.title: Tech Mentor: One on One Computer Help
events.address: 1102 E Santa Clara St San Jose
events.description: Confused by your computer? Get personalized tech assistance. Help is available for basic tasks such as: Printing; Using email; Connecting to Wi-Fi; Creating documents; Accessing library resources. Registering for an appointment is optional. If you register for an appointment, it can start at any time between 3 p.m. and 4:30 pm. Please contact Sarah Kishler at sarah.kishler@sjlibrary.org or 408-808-3075 to let us know what time you would like to come in. When there is space, walk-ins starting between 3 p.m. and 4:30 p.m. are also welcome.
events.blurb: Get personalized help with printing, email, Wi-Fi, documents, or library resources on your computer.

events.title: Edenvale Teens Reach Meeting
events.description: Edenvale will be hosting in-person Teens Reach meetings and will meet every fourth Wednesday of the month from 4-5 PM in the Teen Room. Teens Reach is the youth council for the San José Public Library, providing a key way for young adults to build their leadership skills by developing and participating in library activities, as well as becoming library advisors and advocates. This is a leadership and volunteer service group for teens ages 13-18. Join us and represent the teen community at your local library, meet other teens, take part in decorating the teen room, and learn of other volunteer opportunities at SJPL. If you are new to volunteering with the San Jose Public Library, please visit the Teens Reach: Community Service webpage for more information and make sure to create your online volunteer account (click "Sign Me Up" under Edenvale Branch Library).
events.blurb: Join teens building leadership skills at the Teens Reach youth council meeting at Edenvale Library.

events.title: One-on-One Computer Help with our Tech Mentor
events.address: 1243 San Tomas Aquino Rd. San Jose
events.description: Stop by the West Valley Branch Library for one-on-one computer help with our experienced, friendly Tech Mentor! Our Tech Mentor volunteer can help you with basic computer issues like: Learning the basics of Microsoft Word and Excel; Setting up an email account; Using social networking services like Facebook; Submitting an online job application; downloading an e-book from the library's web site; And much more! No appointment necessary. Patrons will be helped on a first-come, first-served basis. Appointment times may be limited depending on patron demand.
events.attendanceNote: No appointment necessary. Patrons will be helped on a first-come, first-served basis. Appointment times may be limited depending on patron demand.
events.blurb: Stop by for one-on-one help with Microsoft Word, Excel, email setup, and social media basics.

events.title: Reading on the Avenue Book Club
events.description: The Reading on the Avenue Book Club meets on the fourth Wednesday of the month at 7 PM. Newcomers welcome! 2026 Book Selections: November (fiction): The Correspondent by Virginia Evans (note: book club meets 1 week earlier due to Thanksgiving holiday week); December - no meeting in December. 2027 Book Selections: January (non-fiction): Be Ready When the Luck Happens: a memoir by Ina Garten; February (fiction): John of John by Douglas Stuart; March (classic fiction): The Spectator Bird by Wallace Stegner; April (non-fiction): Periodic Tales: A Cultural History of the Elements, From Arsenic to Zinc by Hugh Aldersey-Williams; May (fiction): TBD; June (non-fiction): TBD; July (fiction): TBD; August (non-fiction): TBD; September (classic fiction): TBD; October (non-fiction): TBD; November (fiction): TBD; December - no meeting in December. Additional titles to be selected in March. Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Join the Reading on the Avenue Book Club for its monthly Wednesday evening discussion, where newcomers are welcome.

events.title: BYOB (Bring Your Own Book) Book Club
events.description: Bring a book that you have read that fits into our monthly theme. Come for recommendations, reviews and rapport. We meet in person at the Joyce Ellington Library. Please join us for an afternoon of literary discussion! All are welcome! Upcoming Book Themes: January 28: New Year, New You!: Kick off the new year with a book to inspire or motivate you. Discover a new hobby, dive into a self-help book, or explore health and fitness. February 25: Romance: Fall in love with a classic romance novel or discover a new romantasy author. March 25: Spring Cleaning! Clean out your bookshelf and read a book you have been meaning to read but haven't yet or rediscover a book you may have forgotten about. April 29: Comedy! Find a book that is funny, witty, or clever with themes such as dark humor, satire, or comedic relief. May 20: Movie Adaptation May! Read a book that has been adapted into a movie. Pick an old favorite or a book with a movie coming to theatres soon. June 24: Pride Month. Focus on diverse LGBTQIA+ experiences through contemporary fiction, queer classics, or genre-bending stories. July 22: Graphic Novel Month. Read a manga, graphic novel or comic book. Try a new genre or read a graphic novel that illustrates an old classic. August 26: Beach Reads. Embrace summer reading with a book you would read on the beach or by the pool. September 30: Sci-Fi September. Transition to the "spooky season" with sci-fi reads including apocalyptic, cyberpunk, dystopian, time travel, and more. October 28: Horror/Gothic literature. Explore the dark side of literature with a contemporary, supernatural or gothic tale. November 18: Non-fiction November. Dive into nonfiction and select a true story, memoir or educational text. December 16: Best of 2026. Read a book that was published in 2026.
events.blurb: Share a book you've read that fits the monthly theme and swap recommendations and reviews with fellow readers.

events.title: 1-on-1 Tech Help by Appointment
events.description: Get free one-on-one support with everyday tech questions! Our Tech Mentor can help you with: basic smartphone, tablet, and computer help; setting up and using email; downloading and using apps; making video calls (Zoom, FaceTime, Google Meet, etc.); browsing the internet (search engine basics, making simple searches, etc.); navigating the SJPL website and digital resources. Please note: Tech Mentor support is limited to basic technology questions. Appointments are required. To make an appointment, call 408-808-3073 or email Caitlin Bosworth at caitlin.bosworth@sjlibrary.org.
events.blurb: Sit down one-on-one with a Tech Mentor for help with smartphones, tablets, and computer basics.

events.title: Playdates for Children and Their Caregivers
events.description: Join us every Wednesday for weekly playdates. Kids get to practice early social skills like sharing, taking turns, imitation of play, and joint attention while caregivers get a chance to connect. Don't miss out on this chance to celebrate the joys of play while connecting with other families in the community. It's a wonderful way to learn through play and create lasting memories together! 1st Wednesday: Cars; 2nd Wednesday: Superhero Obstacle Course (ages 3-8); 3rd Wednesday: LEGO Duplo Blocks; 4th Wednesday: Cars; 5th Wednesday: LEGO Duplo Blocks. Recommended for children ages 2 – 6 years old.
events.blurb: Bring your child to Seven Trees Library and practice sharing, turn-taking, and play with other families.

events.title: Family Storytime
events.description: Storytime is a fun and interactive experience designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement activities. This program promotes the joys of reading and learning for children of all ages and their parents/caregivers! Stay after storytime for our Stay and Play session, where kids can enjoy hands-on activities, toys, and social playtime together. Free, with limited capacity. Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of Storytime. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.
events.attendanceNote: Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. A limited number of tickets will be distributed at the Information Desk 30 minutes prior to the start of Storytime.
events.blurb: Gather the family at Joyce Ellington Library for stories, songs, rhymes, and movement in this early literacy storytime.

events.title: Halloween Storytime and Parade
events.description: Bring your costumes and come ready for a Halloween themed storytime followed by our costume parade. Children and families will parade around the library and practice trick-or-treating at different stations. Family Storytime is designed to accommodate a mix of ages and invites the entire family to participate in early literacy activities such as stories, songs, rhymes, fingerplays, and movement. Storytime is a fun and interactive experience for the whole family that promotes the joys of reading and learning for all ages. Treats generously provided by the Friends of the Edenvale Library. Free, with limited capacity. Seating for Storytime is available on a first-come, first-served basis. This program is developed to align with the Early Education Quality Standards.

events.title: Reading Partners One-on-One Reading Tutoring
events.description: Free Reading Help for Students in Grades 1–3. Recommended for students in 2nd and 3rd grade. Give your child extra support to become a stronger, more confident reader! Reading Partners provides free one-on-one reading tutoring with trained volunteer tutors. Students meet twice a week for 45-minute sessions and receive personalized, research-based reading support. Program Dates: September 21, 2026 – May 28, 2027. Space is limited, and applications are reviewed to determine if the program is a good fit for your child. Apply Online — It's Free! Ayuda de lectura Gratis para estudiantes de 1.º a 3.º grado Recomendado para estudiantes de 2.º y 3.º grado. ¡Brinde a su hijo/a apoyo adicional para que se convierta en un lector más seguro y exitoso! Reading Partners ofrece tutoría de lectura individual y gratuita con voluntarios capacitados. Los estudiantes se reúnen dos veces por semana en sesiones de 45 minutos y reciben apoyo personalizado de lectura basado en investigaciones. Fechas del programa: 21 de septiembre de 2026 – 28 de mayo de 2027. El espacio es limitado y las solicitudes serán revisadas para determinar si el programa es adecuado para su hijo/a. Hãy giúp con quý vị nhận thêm sự hỗ trợ để trở thành một người đọc tự tin và thành công hơn! Reading Partners cung cấp hỗ trợ đọc một kèm một hoàn toàn miễn phí với các tình nguyện viên đã được đào tạo. Học sinh tham gia hai buổi mỗi tuần, mỗi buổi 45 phút và nhận được sự hỗ trợ đọc cá nhân dựa trên nghiên cứu. Thời gian chương trình: Ngày 21 tháng 9 năm 2026 – ngày 28 tháng 5 năm 2027. Số lượng chỗ có hạn và các đơn đăng ký sẽ được xem xét để xác định chương trình có phù hợp với con quý vị hay không. Đăng ký trực tuyến — Hoàn toàn MIỄN PHÍ!
events.attendanceNote: Space is limited, and applications are reviewed to determine if the program is a good fit for your child.
events.blurb: Get one-on-one reading help for grades 1-3 from a trained volunteer tutor at Evergreen Library in the afternoon.

events.title: Digital Skills: One-On-One Tech Help for Seniors
events.description: Do you have questions or need assistance with technology? At the Almaden Branch, you can make a 30-minute appointment for assistance with: Learning to use Libby (formerly Overdrive) to read ebooks and listen to e-audiobooks; Accessing non-Overdrive e-books and audiobooks from Boundless, Cloud Library, and Enki; Using Hoopla to read, listen and watch; Accessing the New York Times and/or the San Jose Mercury News online; Accessing and searching Consumer Reports; Learning a new language with Mango; Connecting to Wi-Fi/hotspots; Using Discover & Go to reserve free or reduced tickets to local museums and attractions; Navigating the SJPL website; Checking out a 7-day pass to access Great Courses from Libby or Hoopla; Using the library's pay-to-print system; Walking you through a Digital Skills Building Pathways lesson; And much more! By appointment only. One appointment per week per person. For questions, please call (408) 808-3040 or send an email to ab.sjpl@sjlibrary.org
events.attendanceNote: Using Discover & Go to reserve free or reduced tickets to local museums and attractions
events.blurb: Bring your technology questions to a one-on-one help session designed for seniors at Almaden Library.

events.title: Hindi for Everyday Life
events.description: This is an interactive structured program designed for children ages 5-12 who would like to learn Hindi. Perfectly tailored for learners from all backgrounds whether they hear Hindi at home or are exploring it for the very first time. The curriculum nurtures the four core language skills - Speaking, Listening, Reading and Writing aligned with US Academic Standards and the California World Languages Framework. Children will learn through physical workbooks, worksheets and short audio/visual tools provided for the program, ensuring a rich and engaging experience. Children must be accompanied by an adult caregiver during this workshop.
events.blurb: Learn everyday Hindi phrases and vocabulary with your kids in this interactive Almaden Library session.

events.title: Homework Help for Grades K-6
events.description: Are you a student in grades K-6 who needs help with homework? Tutors are available to help with homework on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday from 4 p.m. - 5:30 p.m. No registration is required. Walk-ins welcome as space allows. Basic school supplies will be provided. Please note: As a parent or caregiver, it is mandatory to stay in the Courtyard or Children's Room while your child participates in the program. Homework Help will not be held on the following dates: September 7; October 12; November 2; November 11; November 23 to November 26; December 21 to January 4. Are you interested in volunteering for Homework Help? Please visit our volunteer page to find out how to be a Homework Help volunteer. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org
events.blurb: Walk in with your K-6 homework and get help from tutors, basic school supplies provided as space allows.

events.title: Mini Makers
events.description: Calling all littles ages 2-5 years old! We'll have three different stations to practice and learn more about fine motor skills. Limited to 30 children. No registration required. Please arrive on time. For children ages 3-5 and their parents and caregivers. Generously sponsored by the Friends of Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (ex. ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.
events.blurb: Let little ones ages 2-5 try three stations that build fine motor skills, with no registration required.

events.title: Wednesday Travel Nights: Discovering America on the Backroads

events.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) for Academic Excellence
events.description: This workshop helps middle and high school students engage with Artificial Intelligence as a meaningful partner in their academic pursuit, rather than a shortcut. Through guided, hands-on learning, participants develop key skills in prompt engineering, research synthesis, and AI-supported organization using tools like Gemini, Notebook LM, and Google Workspace. Grounded in critical thinking and mindful use, the program emphasizes right use, source verification, and proper citation practices. Students learn to evaluate information, build well-supported arguments, and organize ideas into clear, structured academic work. By the end of the session, participants will be confident in using AI responsibly to enhance their learning towards their academic curriculum in an increasingly AI-driven world.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 1st: Topic: Epicurus's Advice: Make Friends and Be Frank with Them "Every friendship is desirable for itself, but it has its origin in personal advantage." Vatican Sayings 23. "We do not need the help of our friends so much as the confidence that our friends will help us." Vatican Sayings 34. "The man continually seeking help is no friend, nor is the one who never links help with friendship. For the one barters kindness for favors, while the other cuts off hope for the future." Vatican Sayings 39. "Of all the things that wisdom provides for the happiness of the whole man, by far the most important is the acquisition of friendship." Principal Doctrine 27. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 6 (pp. 54-65) and 7 (pp. 66-79). Some Questions to Discuss: What are the two main qualities that make a relationship a friendship, according to Emily Austin's analysis of Epicurus's views on friendship? [Austin, 56-7]; Austin says that "a shared sense of what truly matters" [64] is a core condition for friendship. What is the meaning of this condition? Do our current ideas about friendship coincide with those of Epicurus? What do we value in friendship? What is "frank speech" for you? Why can we be uncomfortable with telling a friend the truth? What is the reason for feeling this way? Can we be frank even with ourselves? A friend vs. Psychologist: where does your preference lie and why?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.description: Please join us for a performance by classical guitarist Peter Fletcher, with a program titled "Music of Four Centuries." With a rich history of performances spanning prestigious venues across the United States, Fletcher's captivating music resonates with audiences worldwide. He has been invited to perform at esteemed cultural venues across the US, including Carnegie Hall! Peter will perform music from the new CD, as well as the Bach Chaconne, Usher Waltz by Russian composer Nikita Koshkin, a very special arrangement of the famous Shaker hymn Simple Gifts, and music by Giuliani, Ponce and Tansman. events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Spies Among Us
events.description: This is a rare look into the inner workings of a data-driven surveillance state run by one of the most feared secret police forces the world has ever known – East Germany's Stasi. A personal investigation into family secrets by Peter Keup, a Stasi victim-turned-historian, takes a turn when he contacts the men who ran the system. These are the first dialogues between Stasi officers and a victim ever recorded. Through these encounters a terrifying mosaic is built of the lengths people go to maintain power in a dictatorship, as well as the indomitable human spirit that seeks truth and self-determination. Jamie Coughlin Silverman and Gabriel Silverman are award-winning journalists-turned-documentary filmmakers. Their first feature documentary, TransMilitary, won the Audience Award for Best Documentary at SXSW and received critical acclaim. TransMilitary was represented by Cinetic Media and distributed by Gravitas Ventures. It premiered on Logo TV and Amazon Prime. The film screened at more than 100 film festivals worldwide, and the Silvermans were named to the 2018 Top 10 Filmmakers to Watch list by The Independent. The Silvermans are Gotham (IFP) Documentary Lab Fellows, CNN/Film Independent Episodic Lab Fellows. Their work has been supported by the International Documentary Association, Catapult Film Fund, Jonathan Logan Family Foundation, and Frameline Completion Fund. They are the first recipients of funding from the GLAAD Media Institute. Their production company, SideXSide Studios, is a global documentary firm that specializes in consequential and high-visibility non-fiction storytelling. Prior to SideXSide Studios, the Silvermans worked in leading newsrooms. Gabe was a video journalist at The Washington Post where his work was recognized with more than a dozen awards, including an Edward R. Murrow Award for his investigative work, a White House News Photographers Award for Best Documentary, and two Emmy nominations. Jamie was the supervising producer for USA Today Sports, where she led editorial and branded video content strategy. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch this documentary tracing a Stasi victim's personal investigation into East Germany's surveillance machine.

events.title: Adult Nonfiction Book Discussion: Nothing to Envy: Ordinary Lives in North Korea
events.description: In November, the Adult Nonfiction Book Group will discuss Nothing to Envy: Ordinary Lives in North Korea by Barbara Demick. (2009) Based on Demick's interviews over a seven year period with six North Koreans who escaped the country and the regime. The vast majority of North Koreans know little more of the world beyond their borders than the rest of the world knows about their daily lives under the Kim Jong-il regime. Without easy access to healthcare, experiencing frequent food shortages, life for the average working family in North Korea under Kim Jong-Il's rule is and was grim by Western standards. As of the publication date of this book, ordinary citizens have few if any civil rights and almost no recourse to protest injustice, as complaints and almost any sign of dissatisfaction with the regime could lead to imprisonment. The adult Non-Fiction book group meets on the second Sunday of each month at 11 am in Room 201B. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions. She teaches Visual Storytelling at the Palo Alto Art Center, and at other educational venues. http://danielebd.com/

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For November 15th: Topic: An Epicurean in Public Life: Justice and Injustice "Justice's greatest reward is peace of mind." Fragment 80. "Justice was never an entity in itself. It is a kind of agreement not to harm or be harmed, made when men associate with each other at any time and in communities of any size whatsoever." Principal Doctrine 33. "Injustice is not an evil in itself. Its evil lies in the anxious fear that you will not elude those who have authority to punish such misdeeds." Principal Doctrine 34. "It is impossible to leave the pleasant life without also living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely it is impossible to live sensibly, nobly, and justly without living pleasantly. A person who does not have a pleasant life is not living sensibly, nobly, and justly, and conversely the person who does not have these virtues cannot live pleasantly." Principal Doctrine 5. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 8 (pp. 80-91). Some Questions to Discuss: Based on the ideas expressed in the Principal Doctrines, what is Epicurus's view on the source of justice in society? What is the connection that Epicurus draws between injustice and corrosive desires according to Austin's analysis of his views on injustice? Is it easy to be just? Is it hard to be unjust?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: Master Gardeners: Planning and Planting a Little Fruit Orchard
events.description: Please join us for an informative workshop presented by UC Master Gardeners of Santa Clara County. So you want to plant fruit trees? Excellent! What kind? Are you looking for plums, apricots, peaches, apples or something less common? There are hundreds of varieties of each. How do you choose? How big should the tree be? (There is actually a correct answer!) What are chill hours and how many are good? Semi-dwarf? True dwarf? Multi-graft? How do I plant a new tree? Local nurseries will begin stocking bare root fruit trees in December. Come learn what decisions affect the success of your orchard. Don Bollinger leads the orchard team at the Master Gardener demonstration garden at Martial Cottle Park in South San Jose. He leads year-round hands-on learning and demonstrations of fruit tree management including winter pruning, water, fertilizer, pest management, soil health and fruit variety selection. No need to register, but registering means you will receive a reminder email the day before.

events.title: Don't Get Scammed This Holiday Season
events.description: Online holiday shopping is convenient, but scammers are counting on you to be busy, rushed, and hunting for a good deal. As more of us turn to online shopping and charitable giving this time of year, fraudsters are getting better at looking legitimate. How can you tell if that website is a real store? Is that unbelievable social media deal actually a bargain, or a trap? And when you donate to a cause, how do you know your gift is going where you intended? Join us for a practical presentation that will help you shop and give with confidence. You'll learn how to: Verify that an online store is legitimate before you enter your credit card number; Read and understand product reviews, including how to spot fake or paid reviews; Recognize counterfeit and nonexistent products advertised on social media; Identify charity scams and make sure your donations reach the people and organizations you want to help. You'll leave with simple tips and a few trusted resources to help you stay safe shopping for the holidays and beyond. Keep on hand all season long. Whether you're a seasoned online shopper or just getting started, this program will help you protect your money, your personal information, and your holiday spirit. Bring your questions and your own stories. Your experience might help a neighbor avoid a scam too! Registration is recommended but NOT required. Register in order to receive a reminder email the day before the event.
events.blurb: Learn how to spot holiday shopping scams and protect yourself online at Rinconada Library on Wednesday morning.

events.title: Author Event with Dr. Carol Peyser
events.description: Please join us to hear Dr. Carol Peyser discuss her book, A Hidden Fate (She Writes Press, October 27, 2026), a literary novel interweaving multiple themes: the emotional consequences of genetic foreknowledge, the weight of family secrets and deceptions, overcoming childhood trauma, and the unexpected conflicts of vision and conviction that can emerge in love relationships. The novel has received a starred Kirkus review, and a Book Life reviewer described it as "great for fans of Lisa Genova's Inside the O'Briens and Abraham Verghese's The Covenant of Water." Early in her career, she directed the Huntington's Disease Clinic at Johns Hopkins Hospital right when predictive testing became available to people at risk for the terrible disease. Dr. Peyser saw first-hand how genetic knowledge — and even the possibility of obtaining it — alters a person's relationship to their future and to their family. Interacting with people deciding what they wanted, or might not want, to know about their future seared these issues into her heart. Later, as a geriatric psychiatrist on the Stanford faculty and in private practice in Menlo Park, she saw these questions multiply. Descendants of those with Alzheimer's disease, major depression, and other heritable illnesses grappled with fears about genetic risk — and with the weight of what to keep private, and what to disclose — to whom, and when. These questions of genetic knowledge, secrecy, and their consequences are at the heart of the book. How does wondering what might be coded in our DNA impact us? How does knowing what lies in our genes change us? How are families impacted by the new possibilities genomic testing raises?
events.blurb: Hear author Dr. Carol Peyser speak at an evening author event at Rinconada Library.

events.title: 5, 4, 3, 2, 1: Drawing with Time and Rhythm
events.description: In this one-hour figure-drawing workshop, participants will draw together with pencils for 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute—and sometimes even 30 seconds. We will begin with longer drawing times and slowly move to shorter, faster ones. Participants can try different pencil pressure, movement, and speed as the timing changes. Participants may volunteer to pose for the group. As we draw, we will watch different poses and body movements and follow the changing rhythm together. The timing will be repeated about three times. Participants will make several drawings on 11 × 14-inch paper and one larger drawing on 18 × 24-inch paper, arranging several figures on one sheet. The workshop is open to adults of all levels. No drawing experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including 4B pencils, five sheets of 11 × 14-inch paper, and one sheet of 18 × 24-inch paper for each participant. Duration: 60 minutes
events.blurb: Draw with pencils in timed rounds of 5, 4, 3, 2, and 1 minute, in a one-hour figure-drawing workshop.

events.title: Korean Calligraphy Workshop: Writing Your Name in Hangul with Flow and Rhythm
events.description: In this 90-minute workshop, participants will use calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper to write their names in Hangul. Because Hangul is based on sound, names from many different languages can be written in Hangul according to how they are pronounced. Participants will see how their names look in Hangul and experience the rhythm of Korean writing through brush movement and repetition. Participants can get help writing their names in Hangul along the way. We will begin with simple brush exercises on hanji paper. Participants will practice moving the whole arm, changing the pressure and speed of the brush, and making different kinds of lines. They will then write their names several times, following the movement and rhythm of each brushstroke. At the end of the workshop, participants will write their names on a hanji fan. No previous calligraphy or Korean language experience is needed. Instructor: Sang-ah Choi. Materials: All materials will be provided, including calligraphy brushes, ink, hanji paper, and one hanji fan for each participant. Duration: 90 minutes
events.blurb: Write your name in Hangul using calligraphy brushes, ink, and hanji paper in a 90-minute workshop.

events.title: Documentary: UNAFF presents the Panama Deception
events.description: A riveting Academy Award-winning critique of the government's history of militarization, made all the more timely by the current war on terrorism. 1993 Academy Award, Best Documentary Feature. Read the Acceptance Speech by Barbara Trent. The Panama Deception documents the untold story of the December 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama; the events which led to it; the excessive force used; the enormity of the death and destruction; and the devastating aftermath. The Panama Deception uncovers the real reasons for this internationally condemned attack, presenting a view of the invasion which widely differs from that portrayed by the U.S. media and exposes how the U.S. government and the mainstream media suppressed information about this foreign policy disaster. The Panama Deception includes never before seen footage of the invasion and its aftermath, as well as interviews with both invasion proponents like Gen. Maxwell Thurman, Panamanian President Endara and Pentagon spokesperson Pete Williams, and opponents like U.S. Representative Charles Rangel (D-NY.), Panamanian human rights workers Olga Mejia and Isabel Corro and former Panamanian diplomat Humberto Brown. Network news clips and media critics contribute to a staggering analysis of media control and self-censorship relevant to any news coverage today, particularly during times of war. Among the film's excellent reviews are: "meticulously researched" (Hal Hinson, Washington Post); "outstanding" (Betsy Sherman, Boston Globe); "tough.... Provocative.... Moving.... Beautifully edited" (Vincent Canby, New York Times); and "lays out simply and forcefully the case against the 'official' version" (Peter Rainer, Los Angeles Times). The Empowerment Project (EP) worked on this production for two years. EP first came to prominence in 1988 with the release of the equally acclaimed Coverup: Behind the Iran Contra Affair. EP is a non-profit media resource center committed to democratizing the media. Each year, hundreds of independent filmmakers use EP's edit facilities and other services. Since its August 1992 release, The Panama Deception has played in 80 cities, including an eight-week run in Seattle and a five-week holdover in New York City. The film appeared in video stores in August 1993. It was cablecast on Cinemax in the United States during October of that same year. Many local affiliates of PBS have broadcast the film but national PBS, however, has refused to broadcast the film despite the Congressional mandate explicitly requiring that both sides of controversial issues be included in PBS's overall programming. Internationally, the film has been broadcast in Australia, Canada, Poland, Hong Kong, France, Spain, Portugal, the U.K., Iran, Israel, Finland, Switzerland, Mexico, Argentina, Japan, Norway, the People's Republic of China, S. Korea, Italy, Turkey, Russia, S. Africa, the Netherlands, the Philippines, Algeria, Malaysia, and Czechoslovakia. A ban on the film originally imposed by the Panamanian government was lifted in March 1993, following strong internal and international pressure. Funding for The Panama Deception has been provided, in part, by: Channel Four in London, Rhino Home Video, the I. Roderick MacArthur Foundation, the Rex Foundation, the Peace Development Fund, the National Council of Churches, the Car Eth Foundation, the Vietnam Veterans of America Foundation, the Funding Exchange/Paul Robeson Fund for Film and Video, The Charles Lawrence Keith and Clara Miller Foundation, Essential Information, the Vanguard Public Foundation, Lucille Banta, Michelle Connor, filmmaker Michael Moore and hundreds of individual donors. United Nations Association Film Festival presents documentaries on topical subjects. Jasmina Bojic, Stanford lecturer and International Documentary Film Festival UNAFF founder and director, facilitates discussions with filmmakers and producers.
events.blurb: Watch the Academy Award-winning documentary on Panama and discuss its themes of militarization.

events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 6th: Topic: Epicurus's Challenge to Our Society: Raising a Tranquil Child "The wise man will marry and beget children, as Epicurus tells us in Problems and his work On Nature; but he will marry according to his station in life, whatever it may be." Diogenes Laertius, Lives of Eminent Philosophers, 10:119. "Natural wealth is limited and easily obtained; the riches of idle fancies go on forever." Principal Doctrine 15. "Some men spend their whole life furnishing for themselves the things proper to life without realizing that at our birth each of us was poured a moral brew to drink." Vatican Sayings 30. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Ch. 17 (pp. 180-190). Some Questions to Discuss: In our society, how realistic is Emily Austin's Epicurean plan for raising a child? What are possible impediments to the realization of her plan? What are possible solutions for overcoming these obstacles?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

events.title: Graphic Novel Book Club
events.description: Monthly book discussion on a graphic novel selected by the group! This program is for readers age 16 and up. 2026-2027 titles: September 10 - Ginseng Roots: A Memoir by Craig Thompson (2025) 448 pages. Nonfiction. USA; October 8 - The Winter of the Cartoonist by Paco Roca (author) and Andrea Rosenberg (translator) (2020) 128 pages. Historical nonfiction. Spain. Translation; November 12 - It's Not What You Thought It Would Be by Lizzy Stewart (2021) 168 pages. Fiction. Coming-of-age story of young women. The author, originally from Scotland, lives in London, England. December 10 - Impossible People: A Completely Average Recovery Story by Julia Wertz (2023) 320 pages. Nonfiction. Julia Wertz lives in Sonoma County; January 14 - Love Languages by James Albon (2025) 176 pages. Queer romance graphic novel set in France. Fiction. James Albon is from Scotland. February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. Fiction, based on real events. Story of a Korean family separated by the war. Translation. May 13 - You and a Bike and a Road by Eleanor Davis (2024) 172 pages. Nonfiction. A two-wheeled journey across the landscape of America, and through the heart and mind of an artist. USA. Titles can be borrowed from the Palo Alto City Library and through our Link+ system - click on the links above or search in our catalog for more information. Meetings are held in person in the Midtown Room at Mitchell Park Library and facilitated by Danièle Archambault. Danièle Archambault, Ph. D. (Linguistics), is a researcher, author, and educator who is interested in comics as a way to document a society's cultural and linguistic landscape. Originally from Montreal, Quebec, she now lives in Palo Alto, where she is an artist in residence at the Cubberley Artist Studio Program, a program of the City of Palo Alto. In the past few years, she has published several full-color comic books, graphic novels, and electronic books. Ms. Archambault is a regular guest speaker on documenting culture and dialects through comics at various educational and cultural institutions.
