events.title: Philosophy for Life
events.description: Philosophy for Life: A friendly reading and discussion group at the library, exploring big ideas about how we live and what we value. Why do we believe that success means constant hustle, that more is always better, or that everyone must go it alone? What other ways of thinking might help us make sense of everyday life? Together, we'll read accessible texts from different philosophical traditions and enjoy open, respectful conversations about the assumptions shaping our world. Open to adults, young adults and seniors. No background in philosophy required—just curiosity and a willingness to talk and listen. We'll read the following books: Living for Pleasure: An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin; A Guide to the Good Life: The Ancient Art of Stoic Joy by William B. Irvine; Choosing Freedom: A Kantian Guide to Life by Karen Stohr; On Being and Becoming: an Existentialist Approach to Life by Jennifer Anna Gosetti-Ferencei; Blooming in the Ruins: How Mexican Philosophy Can Guide Us Toward the Good Life by Carlos Alberto Sánchez. We'll meet every first and third Sunday at the Rinconada Library from 3:30 PM to 4:45 PM. *A detailed list of readings for each meeting can be found on the library calendar under the date of the corresponding meeting. In order to ensure an engaging discussion in which all can participate, attendance is limited to registrants. If the maximum capacity has been reached, please join the waitlist and you will be notified if you have been added to the group. Also, if you need to cancel your registration, please do so by 6:00 PM the Thursday before the meeting so people on the waitlist can be registered. Moderated by Natalia & Lottie, PACL staff. For December 20th: Topic: Becoming an Epicurean? "In other occupations, the reward comes with difficulty after their completion, but in philosophy delight coincides with knowledge. For enjoyment does not come after learning, but learning and enjoyment come together." Vatican Sayings 27. "We must not pretend to be philosophers, but be philosophers in truth. For we do not stand in need of the appearance of health but of true health." Vatican Sayings 54. "By love of true philosophy we are delivered from every disturbing and painful desire." Fragment 66. "The most important consequence of self-sufficiency is freedom." Vatican Sayings 77. "The impassive soul disturbs neither itself nor others." Vatican Sayings 79. Literature: Living for Pleasure. An Epicurean Guide to Life by Emily A. Austin. Chs. 23 (pp. 241-251) and 24 (pp. 252-266). Some Questions to Discuss: In your opinion, which of Epicurus's ideas, if any, have not lost their currency and would be beneficial to our society? What needs to be done to implement them? What challenges may their implementation face?
events.blurb: Join a reading and discussion group about big ideas, including why many people tie success to constant hustle and going it alone.

February 11 - Illegal: A Graphic Novel by Eoin Colfer (Author), Andrew Donkin (Author), Giovanni Rigano (Illustrator) (2018) 144 pages. Fiction, based on real events. It explores the current plight of undocumented immigrants. March 11 - More Weight: A Salem Story by Ben Wickey (2025) 532 pages. Historical nonfiction. The book explores the infamous Salem witch trials and the long shadows they cast more than 300 years later. USA; April 8 - The Waiting by Keum Suk Gendry-Kim (2021) 247 pages. events.description: Watch some Halloween classics at your library! Bring a blanket and a pillow for a more laid back viewing, or sit in the chairs provided. October 16th: Beetlejuice (1988); October 23rd: The Addams Family (1991); October 30th: The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993).

events.title: Game Zone
events.description: Are you an expert at video, board, and card games? Do you want to demonstrate your skills, or just want to learn the basics? Or maybe you'd like to sink the 8 ball at a game of pool? Join us in the Teen Room at the Hillview Branch Library if you want to play video, board, and card games, play some pool, or just hang out! Free. No registration required.

events.title: Family Craft: Pom Pom Photo Frames
events.description: Create and decorate a pom pom photo frame! Children ages 4–11 are invited to make a unique design using popsicle sticks, glue, sequins, buttons, and pom poms. All materials will be provided. Family Craft events are designed for children and their adult companions to enjoy together. Crafts will be available while supplies last, so please arrive on time.

events.title: Reading to Children with Aysha
events.description: Participating in the Reading to Children program is a great way for children to develop their imagination and spark a love for books, reading and learning. events.blurb: Read one-on-one or in a small group with volunteer Aysha to build reading confidence and love of books.

events.title: DIY Marble Mazes
events.description: Challenge yourself with a dexterity-testing marble maze that you design and build! You'll use everyday objects to create a maze, then tilt and tip marbles through from start to finish! Rebuild and redesign to make the labyrinth of your dreams, then trade with your friends and find out who the real maze master is! Free. No registration required.
events.blurb: Design and build your own marble maze from everyday objects, then tilt it to guide marbles through.

events.title: Medicare Mysteries Solved!
events.description: Are you getting ready to apply for Medicare and are confused by the different plans to choose from? Join Sandra Karol, MS, RDMS, RVT, for a monthly workshop and learn more about the different plans that will work best for you and your family. Please register directly with Sandy at isail2@earthlink.net. Attendee limit is 10 people per session.
events.blurb: Learn about Medicare plan options from Sandra Karol in this monthly workshop.

events.description: Free. Placement test and registration required. Learn basic reading, writing, speaking, & listening skills with your library for free! Call the library at (408) 808-3056.

All equipment provided.

events.title: Festival of Lights: A Diwali Celebration
events.description: Join us at the Mitchell Park Community Center, as we celebrate Diwali! Enjoy fun activities for all ages including: Ongoing from 2-4 PM: Henna with teaching artist Rachel-Anne Palacios (Adobe Room; henna line closes at 3:30 PM!) Rangoli (chalk coloring craft outside in the Courtyard); Crafts (in Adobe Room); All activities available while supplies last! Performance from 2:30-3:30 PM in El Palo Alto Room by Noorani Dance. Rachel-Anne Palacios is an Afro-Chicana Oakland native, multi-cultural arts educator, and self-taught folk artist. She has been teaching art workshops and classes at Bay Area schools and libraries for over a decade and a half and her lessons and projects are inspired by indigenous cultures and traditional art from around the world. Noorani Dance, founded in 2016 by international Kathak artist, Farah Yasmeen Shaikh, exemplifies Farah's unique artistic expression and vision coupled with the classical and innovative influence and style of Farah's Guru, the late Pandit Chitresh Das. "Noorani" means bright or luminous, with a dual meaning of enlightenment. With Kathak dance as their medium, Noorani Dance is committed to enlightening minds and hearts through the arts.
events.blurb: Get henna from teaching artist Rachel-Anne Palacios and join Diwali activities at Mitchell Park Community Center.

events.title: Cielo Hotel Valencia Rooftop Holiday Experience
events.description: November 27, 2026. Beginning November 27, join us Tuesday through Saturday from 5:00–9:00 pm, for winter evenings at Cielo Rooftop at Hotel Valencia. The experience will be closed Sundays and Mondays. This holiday season, Cielo Rooftop transforms into an intimate winter retreat high above Santana Row, where seasonal warmth and elevated style come together against the backdrop of the Santa Cruz Mountains. Settle in beneath the open sky and enjoy seasonal cocktails and a curated menu of winter-inspired bites in a warm and inviting rooftop setting. Thoughtful seasonal touches and the glow of the city below create the perfect atmosphere for festive gatherings, date nights, or simply savoring the season.
events.blurb: Spend a winter evening on the Cielo Rooftop at Hotel Valencia, open Tuesday through Saturday from 5:00 to 9:00 pm.

events.title: Line Dancing with Sandy and Kent
events.description: Join Sandy and Kent for a family-friendly line dancing class! Exercise your brain and body and enhance your balance while dancing to a variety of international music. No partner needed and beginners welcome! You are welcome to practice before and after by checking out their special playlist for this class. This class will take place in the Mitchell Park Bowl. (In the event of rain, the class will move to the Midtown Room inside the Mitchell Park Library.) Sandy and Kent have taught line dancing throughout the Bay Area for ten years. Learn more about them on their YouTube channel. Registration is not required. If you register, you will get an email reminder for the program including a link to the class playlist to practice.
events.blurb: Learn line dancing steps with Sandy and Kent to international music, no partner or experience needed.

events.title: Location Change: Mindfulness Meditation
events.description: Note: The December 5th meditation session will be at the Palo Alto Art Center. This session is open to all ages. Children under 10 years old must be accompanied by an adult. Come and improve your mental and physical health in mindfulness meditation sessions led by Phuong Pham. Each session is 30 minutes of sitting meditation and 15 minutes of releasing meditation followed by 15 minutes of group sharing and Q&A. It is open to all levels of experience and no registration is required. Participants are encouraged to bring their own yoga mats and/or meditation cushions. Chairs are available for those who do not bring them. Phuong is a Buddhist nun experienced in leading mindfulness meditation. You can learn more about Phuong here and can watch her meditation videos on the library's YouTube channel here.
events.blurb: Join Phuong Pham for a mindfulness meditation session at the Art Center Meeting Room.

events.title: Watershed Habitat of the Steelhead Nature Walk
events.description: Join a Naturalist and learn about the Steelhead life cycle, riparian habitat and challenges faced in Stevens Creek. We will walk through history and view our ecosystem through the lens of this phenomenal species. You and your child will identify aquatic insects as a measure of water quality. The hike is approximately one mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. All attendees must register and children must be accompanied by an adult. $25 Resident | $32 Non-resident
events.blurb: Walk along Stevens Creek with a naturalist to learn about the Steelhead life cycle and riparian habitat.

events.title: Noon Year's Eve Celebration!
events.description: Not planning to stay up until midnight on New Year's Eve with your little ones? Then join us for a "Noon" Year's Eve celebration! We will count down to noon on Thursday, December 31, complete with a "ball and bubble" drop. We'll ring in the new year with crafts, dancing and music, so bring your party hats and noisemakers! Come dressed in party attire if you'd like! *This event will be held in the Adobe Room of the Mitchell Park Community Center.
events.blurb: Count down to noon with your little ones, with a ball and bubble drop, so no one has to stay up until midnight.

events.title: Join-A-Ranger: Bird ID and Guided Hike
events.description: The Park Rangers invite you to learn about the birds living in our riparian habitat and how to ID them! Walk the trails to see the environment they live in and maybe catch a glimpse of a Red-Shouldered Hawk, Screech Owl, or more! All attendees must register and an adult must accompany children. The hike is approximately one-quarter mile on a combination of dirt trails and paved paths. $10 Resident | $13 Non-resident
events.blurb: Walk the riparian trails with Park Rangers on Saturday morning, learning to identify local birds and watching for hawks and owls.

events.title: Alice, Formerly of Wonderland
events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming-of-age story revealing the truth behind the fairy tale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll's classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria's youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this a cappella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.
events.blurb: Watch the coming-of-age story of Alice Liddell and Prince Leopold unfold onstage at Lucie Stern Theatre.

events.description: Seven-time Emmy Award-winning writer Mark Saltzman illuminates the beautiful coming-of-age story revealing the truth behind the fairy tale between Alice Liddell—the real-life inspiration of Lewis Carroll's classic tale—and Prince Leopold, Queen Victoria's youngest son. Brimming with wit and emotional spark, this a cappella musical weaves between Victorian reality and Wonderland whimsy, revealing a tender connection shaped by duty, distance, and the ache of what might have been. Perfect for the holiday season, Alice, Formerly of Wonderland glows with warmth, longing, and just enough wonder to feel like a gift.

events.title: Shane
events.description: A Wild West classic. Honoring the original while cracking it wide open, Karen Zacarias' storytelling is a living, breathing world of the American frontier as told by voices too often left out of the legend. The play unfolds in the vast Wyoming prairies, where families fighting for their land are pushed to the breaking point by forces determined to drive them out. Featuring Bay Area theatre veteran Aldo Billingslea as the fabled cowboy, Shane reminds us that true heroism isn't always about the fastest draw—it's about doing the right thing when it counts.
events.blurb: Watch a Wild West drama unfold on the Wyoming prairie, told through voices often left out of the legend.

events.title: Beautiful: The Carole King Musical
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Feel the earth move under your feet! Soulful and irresistible, this feel-good musical tells the true story of the woman behind the soundtrack of our lives. From teenage songwriter to chart-topping legend, Carole King finds her voice in a world that wasn't always ready to hear it. Set against the vibrant music scene of the 1950s and 1960s, the journey follows love, resilience, the sort of friendships that shape a life—and a career that changed music forever. Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.

events.description: Feel the earth move under your feet! Soulful and irresistible, this feel-good musical tells the true story of the woman behind the soundtrack of our lives. From teenage songwriter to chart-topping legend, Carole King finds her voice in a world that wasn't always ready to hear it. Set against the vibrant music scene of the 1950s and 1960s, the journey follows love, resilience, the sort of friendships that shape a life—and a career that changed music forever. Featuring a thrilling lineup of iconic hits including "You've Got a Friend," "It's Too Late," and "You Make Me Feel Like a Natural Woman," Beautiful makes you laugh, tear up, and leave the theatre humming all the way home.
events.blurb: Watch the true story of Carole King's rise from teenage songwriter to chart-topping icon unfold in song at Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts.

events.title: Dracula
events.venue: Mountain View Center for the Performing Arts
events.description: Sink your teeth into the ultimate Halloween thrill. Steven Dietz's adaptation of the timeless classic seduces with elegance and suspense, turning the legendary vampire tale into a high-octane theatrical ride. Bold, chilling, and wickedly smart, the story draws you into a world where reason clashes with superstition and love becomes dangerously intoxicating. This Dracula keeps you leaning forward—never quite sure who holds the power, or what darkness waits just out of sight.
events.blurb: Watch this staged retelling of Dracula pull you into its shadowy, suspenseful world.

events.title: 2026 Cupertino Community Service Awards
events.address: Quinlan Community Center, 10185 N. Stelling Road, 95014
events.description: The third annual Cupertino Community Service Awards will take place on Wednesday, October 28. This ceremony will recognize the 2026 Crest Awards (Cupertino Recognizes Extra Steps Taken), and Commissioners who served on a City Commission. Doors open at 5:30 p.m. The program starts at 6 p.m. RSVP is required. Registration will open for the public on Monday, September 21.
events.blurb: Attend the Cupertino Community Service Awards ceremony honoring Crest Award recipients and city commissioners.

events.title: Breakfast with Santa
events.address: Quinlan Community Center, 10185 North Stelling Road, 95014
events.description: You and your family are invited to a festive breakfast celebration with Santa! Enjoy delicious North Pole pancakes prepared by Santa's elves, take photos with Santa, and explore a holiday workshop filled with crafts and activities for children. Three seatings: 8:30 a.m., 9:30 a.m., 10:30 a.m. Registration opens in late July.
events.blurb: Eat North Pole pancakes, snap photos with Santa, and join holiday crafts with your family.

events.address: The Tech Interactive, 201 S Market St, San Jose, CA 95113
events.description: Halloween at the museum with costumes, trick-or-treat stations, spooky science activities, photo ops and a slime workshop. Laser shows in the Dome Theater (Halloween Spooktacular at 4:30 and 5:15 p.m., Stranger Things at 6 p.m.) cost extra. Tickets are $38 for adults and $28 for children, seniors and students.

events.address: Quinlan Community Center, 10185 North Stelling Road, Cupertino, CA, 95014
events.description: Kick off the holiday season at the City's annual Community Tree Lighting! Enjoy the moment the tree is illuminated with hundreds of twinkling lights, live music from a local choir, and festive holiday cheer. After the tree lighting, families can visit Santa and take photos.
events.blurb: Watch the community tree light up, hear a local choir sing, and visit Santa for photos afterward.

events.blurb: See a working forge in action and learn blacksmithing basics from an experienced smith at McClellan Ranch.

events.description: A free, family-friendly festival celebrating San Jose's indigenous, Spanish, Mexican, and multicultural history, kicking off the city's 250th anniversary with hands-on activities, historic home tours, local art, and cultural performances.
events.blurb: Tour the historic adobe homes, join hands-on activities, and catch local art and cultural performances marking San Jose's 250th.

events.title: Location Change: Meditation with Sara
events.description: Note: The November 7th meditation session will be at the Palo Alto Art Center. Join us for a guided meditation experience with Sara. Welcome to all experience levels. This will be a seated meditation session that lasts about 30 minutes.
events.blurb: Settle into a seated guided meditation with Sara at the Art Center Meeting Room.

events.address: Lakewood Branch Library and Learning Center, 760 Lakechime Drive, Sunnyvale, CA 94089
events.description: The City of Sunnyvale celebrates the opening of its first full-service branch library with a ribbon-cutting, remarks from city leaders, and family activities including Maker Lab demonstrations; Halloween costumes encouraged.
events.blurb: Join the ribbon-cutting for Sunnyvale's new Lakewood Branch Library, with remarks, Maker Lab demos, and family activities.

events.title: Free Confidential Document Shredding

events.title: JTown Skate Day and Halloween in Japantown
events.address: San Jose Japantown, 5th & Jackson Street, San Jose, CA 95112
events.description: A free, family-friendly Halloween celebration in San Jose Japantown featuring a skateboarding demo with Judi Oyama, skate lessons, crafts, a sticker rally, and the opening of Judi Oyama's art exhibition at JAMsj.
events.blurb: Watch Judi Oyama's skate demo, try a lesson, make crafts, and check out her new art exhibition opening at JAMsj.

events.title: Congressional Gold Medal Dedication and Community Gathering
events.venue: Japanese American Museum of San Jose
events.address: Japanese American Museum of San Jose, 535 N. Fifth St, San Jose, CA 95112
events.description: Community gathering and monument dedication honoring Japanese American veterans of the 442nd Regimental Combat Team who received the Congressional Gold Medal; medal recipients, relatives, and friends are invited.
events.blurb: Join medal recipients, relatives, and friends as the Japanese American Museum dedicates the Congressional Gold Medal to 442nd veterans.

events.title: Fiddler on the Roof
events.description: Fiddler on the Roof: Tradition meets revolution in Opera San Jose's new production of Fiddler on the Roof. In a vibrant Jewish shtetl on the eve of upheaval, Tevye, the enduring dairyman, grapples with his daughters' dreams of love while clinging to the customs that provide his world's structural integrity.
events.blurb: Watch Opera San Jose's production of Fiddler on the Roof at the California Theatre.

events.title: Lecture: Native Histories of the Collapse of the California Missions
events.address: Mission Branch Library, 1098 Lexington St, Santa Clara, CA 95050
events.description: Archaeologist Lee Panich explains how the ancestors of today's Ohlone community navigated the collapse of the California mission system between 1821 and 1846. Part of the Lectures in the Library series.
events.blurb: Hear archaeologist Lee Panich explain how Ohlone ancestors navigated the collapse of the California mission system between 1821 and 1846.

events.title: 'The Golden Age' or 'the Dark Time of the Plots': Iraq and Syria in the 1950s | Matthieu Rey
events.description: 1946. The last French soldier left Syria. A few months before, Tawfiq al-Suweidi, the Iraqi Prime Minister, introduced a set of laws to protect constitutional freedoms and legalize political parties.
events.blurb: Hear Matthieu Rey's talk on Iraq and Syria in the 1950s, starting from the post-1946 political party and constitutional freedom laws.

events.title: Quilling Craft Club
events.address: Central Park Library - Heritage Pavilion, 2635 Homestead Rd, Santa Clara, California 95051
events.description: A hands-on workshop teaching the art of paper quilling, suitable for beginners and those looking to refresh their skills. All supplies are provided, but registration is required due to limited space.
events.attendanceNote: Registration is required; space is limited. Use the form on the library's event page.
events.blurb: Learn paper quilling techniques in a hands-on workshop for beginners and returning crafters.

events.title: Wonders of Cherry Springs
events.address: VTA Park & Ride lot at Camden Avenue @ Highway 85
events.description: Join Docent Naturalists Greg Azevedo and Emma Finter for a leisurely paced hike at a limited-access area. You'll travel in a single loop, traversing grasslands, mixed evergreen forest, and chaparral.
events.blurb: Hike a limited-access loop through grasslands, forest, and chaparral with docent naturalists at Cherry Springs.

events.title: Wildcard Ramble at Rancho
events.address: Meet near the restroom at the bottom of the hill in the preserve parking lot farthest to the right
events.description: Why "wildcard"? Because you and other participants will help choose the route together depending on the weather, trail conditions, and how you feel. Here's one possibility: Will the creek have water?
events.blurb: Help choose your own route with fellow hikers based on weather and trail conditions at Rancho.

events.title: Constructing Utopias: China's New Town Movement in the 21st Century
events.description: Amid groundbreaking political reforms and the largest mass migration in human history, China created over 3,800 new towns to house its burgeoning urban population and sustain rapid economic growth.
events.blurb: Hear a Monday noon talk at Encina Hall on how China built over 3,800 new towns to house its growing urban population.

events.title: Artist Talk with Hiroyuki Murase
events.address: 450 Jane Stanford Way, Building 460, Stanford, CA 94305
events.description: Hiroyuki Murase is the CEO and Creative Director of the textile brand suzusan, bringing the beauty and sustainable ethos of traditional Japanese shibori dyeing to the world of contemporary fashion.
events.blurb: Hear Hiroyuki Murase, CEO and Creative Director of textile brand suzusan, talk about bringing traditional Japanese shibori dyeing into contemporary fashion.

events.title: Morning Meander: Meadow to Farm
events.address: Meet near the restroom at the bottom of the hill in the preserve parking lot farthest to the right
events.description: Feel refreshed on a late-winter morning stroll with Docent Naturalists Laura Levin, Emma Finter, and Marie-Anne Neimat through meadow and creekside habitats to visit the historic Deer Hollow Farm.
events.blurb: Stroll with docent naturalists through meadow and creekside habitats to the historic Deer Hollow Farm.

events.title: Tangling the Digital: Weaving, Printmaking, Computing
events.description: Free exhibition exploring weaving, printmaking, and computing at Coulter Art Gallery in the McMurtry Building. On view September 29–December 4, 2026, Monday–Friday, 1–5 PM; closed November 23–27.
events.blurb: Visit a free exhibition exploring weaving, printmaking, and computing at Coulter Art Gallery.

events.title: Trees & Friends
events.description: Join Docent Naturalists Nick Yatsko, Mallik K., and Catherine Xun on this moderately paced exploration of the various trees and understory plants that make this preserve so green and biodiverse.
events.blurb: Walk a moderately paced trail with docent naturalists spotting trees and understory plants at Bear Creek Redwoods.

events.title: 10 Laws of Finance for Business Owners
events.venue: Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. Library
events.address: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Library, SJPL Works, San Jose, CA
events.description: A free two-hour in-person workshop from the Silicon Valley SBDC teaching business owners ten key financial decisions to understand, measure, and improve for their company's financial health.
events.blurb: Learn ten key financial decisions business owners should track in this two-hour SBDC workshop at the library.

events.title: Newt Knowledge
events.address: preserve parking lot on Montebello Road
events.description: Join Docent Naturalists Roberta and Jaime Cavazos and Melissa Hero on a family-friendly hike looking for one of the most charismatic amphibians calling the Santa Cruz Mountains home: Newts!
events.blurb: Search for newts on a family-friendly hike with docent naturalists at Picchetti Ranch Preserve.

events.title: Tails & Twilight Trails
events.address: Prospect Parking Area on Prospect Road in Cupertino
events.description: Join Docent Naturalists Ani Agahian, Mary Ann Frank, and Minh Pham for a serene sunset adventure at Hunters Point, a 900-foot-high hilltop with breathtaking views of the Santa Clara Valley.
events.blurb: Watch the sunset from Hunters Point's 900-foot hilltop with docent naturalists at Fremont Older.

events.title: Sawmills to Seminary to Open Space
events.description: Explore the layered history of this preserve—from Indigenous stewardship to sawmill, estate, seminary, and open space—with Docent Naturalists John Seyfarth, Catherine Xun, and Nick Yatsko.
events.blurb: Walk through Bear Creek Redwoods' layered history, from Indigenous stewardship to sawmill and seminary, with docent naturalists.
